text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past purchases as continuing interest in related products, brands, or entertainment styles without sufficiently identifying the user's current purpose.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they continue a specific, repeated interest, such as a favored artist, musical sound, seasonal theme, or fastener type.",
    "Related products appeal when they add a useful capability to equipment or materials the user already owns."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related products compete with stronger matches despite lacking a concrete connection to the user's current task, listening preference, or viewing interest.",
    "Recommendations repeat functions already covered by recent purchases or suggest older equivalents without an evident additional benefit.",
    "Specialized accessories and supplies are treated as plausible purchases without sufficient evidence of compatible equipment, matching dimensions, or appropriate quantities."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared product domain, brand ecosystem, artist era, or broad genre appears to substitute for a specific reason to choose an item.",
    "A previous purchase appears to imply continued demand for similar products even when it may have satisfied the underlying need."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent, repeated, specific interests deserve more weight than isolated or older interactions when identifying current intent.",
    "Practical choices depend on compatibility, scale, quantity, and whether an item complements existing ownership.",
    "Entertainment choices depend on specific sound, story, tone, format, and occasion rather than broad familiarity alone.",
    "Sparse or unidentified histories provide limited support for confident preference extrapolation."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top-ranked items too often have a broad historical association without a specific current use or preference match strong enough to motivate a choice.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked items users would choose now, distinguishing immediate choices from merely plausible matches.",
    "The frequency of rejected top-ranked items attributed to redundant ownership, incompatibility, excessive quantity, or an unsupported project assumption.",
    "The frequency with which users prefer a lower-ranked item because it better matches a recent specific interest than higher-ranked broadly related items.",
    "The proportion of feedback that cannot establish relevance because item or history information is unidentified, tracked separately from explicit preference mismatch."
  ]
}
